get.description:

Returns counts of:
- pending_upload: Files extracted but not yet uploaded to Graph
- uploaded: Files successfully uploaded to Graph

- in_progress: Upload work items currently being processed

post.description:
Manually trigger Graph backfill for pre-crawled items.

This creates upload work items for all extracted files that haven't
been uploaded to Microsoft Graph yet. Useful when:
- Graph upload was disabled during initial crawl
- You want to re-upload files that were skipped
- Recovering from a failed Graph connector configuration

Manually trigger Graph cleanup for uploaded items.

This creates cleanup work items to remove all previously uploaded
files from Microsoft Graph. Use this when:
- Removing a share's content from Graph
- Cleaning up after disabling Graph upload
- Resetting Graph state for a share

Re-queue failed Graph upload work items for retry.

This resets all failed upload work items back to pending status,
clearing their retry count so they can be processed again. Use when:
- Network issues caused temporary upload failures
- Graph API was temporarily unavailable
- Configuration issues have been resolved

Force re-upload of completed Graph upload work items.

This resets all completed upload work items back to pending status so they
will be re-processed. Use after changing share settings (e.g. acl_override_mode)
that require files to be re-uploaded to Graph.

get.description:
Get current setup status.

Returns setup completion status and list of completed/required steps.
Also indicates if the application is in license reconfiguration mode.

post.description:
Mark setup as complete.

Call this endpoint after all required configuration steps are finished
to exit setup mode and start normal operation.

**Prerequisites**:
- DATABASE_URL environment variable must be set
- License must be configured (via API or NETAPP_CONNECTOR_LICENSE env var)

Optional steps (can be configured later):
- Graph configuration (only needed for Microsoft Graph/Copilot integration)
- SSL/TLS settings
- Proxy settings

Configure NetApp Connector license.

**Required**: License key for the connector

When in license reconfiguration mode, this endpoint will validate the new license
and trigger an automatic restart if the license is valid.

**Example**:
```json
{
    "license_key": "your-license-key-here"
}
```

get.description:
Get current license status and connector ID.

This endpoint is especially useful when the application is in license
reconfiguration mode due to a license mismatch or missing license.

Returns:
- connector_id: The ID used for license validation (provide this to licensing support)
- license_configured: Whether a license key is present
- license_valid: Whether the license is valid for this connector
- error_message: Details about any license validation error
- in_reconfiguration_mode: Whether the app is in license reconfiguration mode

Get current Microsoft Graph settings.

Returns the current Graph configuration (client_secret is not returned for security).

post.description:
Configure Microsoft Graph credentials for Copilot integration.

**Note**: This step is OPTIONAL. Only configure if you want to integrate with
Microsoft Graph/Copilot. If you only want to index files to the local database,
you can skip this step.

**Required** (if configuring Graph):
- tenant_id: Azure AD Tenant ID
- client_id: Application (client) ID
- client_secret: Client secret value

**Optional**:
- connector_id: Custom connector ID (default: "netappneo")
- connector_name: Display name for the connector
- connector_description: Description of the connector

**Example**:
```json
{
    "tenant_id": "your-tenant-id",
    "client_id": "your-client-id",
    "client_secret": "your-client-secret",
    "connector_id": "netappneo",
    "connector_name": "NetApp NEO Connector",
    "connector_description": "SMB Share Integration"
}
```

get.description:
Get current MCP OAuth settings.

Returns the current MCP OAuth configuration (client_secret is not returned for security).

post.description:
Configure MCP OAuth settings for Claude Desktop and MCP client authentication.

This configures OAuth 2.0 authentication for the MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint,
allowing Claude Desktop and other MCP clients to authenticate using Microsoft Entra ID.

**Required**:
- tenant_id: Azure AD Tenant ID
- client_id: Application (client) ID from Azure App Registration
- client_secret: Client secret value

**Optional**:
- audience: Token audience for validation (defaults to client_id if not specified)

**Example**:
```json
{
    "tenant_id": "your-tenant-id",
    "client_id": "your-mcp-client-id",
    "client_secret": "your-mcp-client-secret",
    "audience": "api://your-mcp-client-id"
}
```

**Note**: The MCP OAuth configuration is separate from the Graph API configuration.
MCP OAuth is used for authenticating MCP clients (like Claude Desktop),
while Graph API credentials are used for Microsoft 365 Copilot integration.

post.description:

get.description:
Get current SSL/TLS settings.

Returns the current SSL verification, timeout, and custom CA certificate status.

post.description:
Configure SSL/TLS settings for Microsoft Graph connections.

**Optional**:
- verify_ssl: Enable/disable SSL verification (default: true)
- timeout: Request timeout in seconds (default: 30)
- ca_certificate: Full PEM-encoded CA certificate content (including -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----)
- allow_legacy_certificates: Allow CA certificates without keyUsage X.509 extension (default: false)

**Example**:
```json
{
    "verify_ssl": true,
    "timeout": 30,
    "ca_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIDXTCCAkWgAwIBAgIJAKJ...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
    "allow_legacy_certificates": false
}
```

**Note**: The certificate content will be stored in the database and combined with the default
certifi CA bundle. No file system access or volume mounts required.

**Legacy Certificate Mode**: Some corporate proxy CA certificates don't include the keyUsage
X.509 extension, which Python 3.13+ requires by default. Setting `allow_legacy_certificates: true`
disables this strict checking. Only enable this if you trust your proxy CA and cannot obtain
a properly configured certificate.

get.description:
Get current proxy settings.

Returns the current proxy configuration (password is not returned for security).

post.description:
Configure proxy settings for Microsoft Graph connections.

**Optional**:
- proxy_url: Proxy server URL (e.g., "http://proxy.example.com:8080")
- proxy_username: Proxy authentication username
- proxy_password: Proxy authentication password

**Example**:
```json
{
    "proxy_url": "http://proxy.example.com:8080",
    "proxy_username": "user",
    "proxy_password": "pass"
}
```

**Note**: To remove proxy configuration, call with all fields set to null.

Hot-reload SSL/proxy settings without restarting the service.

This endpoint reloads SSL and proxy settings from the database and applies them
to the OAuth provider, allowing settings changes to take effect immediately
without requiring a service restart.

**Use Cases**:
- After configuring SSL settings via POST /api/v1/setup/ssl
- After configuring proxy settings via POST /api/v1/setup/proxy
- When testing different SSL/proxy configurations

**Note**: This only affects the API service's OAuth provider (used for MCP authentication).
The worker service will need to be restarted separately to pick up new settings
for Microsoft Graph API calls.

Reset setup state (for testing or reconfiguration).

**Warning**: This will reset all setup progress. Use with caution.

post.description:
Perform a complete factory reset of the connector.

**DANGER: This is a destructive operation that cannot be undone!**

This will:
- Delete ALL shares and their configurations
- Delete ALL file metadata and inventory
- Delete ALL work queue items
- Delete ALL users (including admin)
- Delete ALL operation logs
- Reset ALL system configuration (except encryption key if preserve_encryption_key=true)
- Create a new admin account with a new auto-generated password

**Use Cases:**
- Fresh start after testing
- Decommissioning and recommissioning
- Recovery from corrupted state

**Requirements:**
- Must set `confirm: true` in the request body

FileListResponse.title: FileListResponse
FileListResponse.description:
Response model for file listing with pagination.

``total_count`` and ``total_size`` are optional: callers can suppress them
with ``?include_counts=false`` to skip the cross-partition aggregates that
dominate request latency at billion-row scale. ``total_pages``, ``has_next``,
and ``has_previous`` are derived from page-vs-returned-rows when totals are
omitted, so basic pagination still works without them.

``next_cursor`` is set when the request used keyset pagination
(``?after_modified_time=...``); pass it back as the next call's cursor to
walk through millions of rows in O(log N) per page rather than O(N) per
deep-offset page.
